answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring each identity to sustain a live opal memory-hard sequential plume of unique state proofs bound to non-shareable hardware. An attacker spawning 200 sable clones must dedicate separate 32GB RAM pools to each plume, costing ~6.4TB total that cannot be pooled; an honest agent pays only its single plume. The mechanism fails if cheap virtualization allows memory overcommit across clones.
